advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the new corpus-exclusion test take the `pyproject` fixture (or re-check `_PYPROJECT.is_file()`/skip) so it skips rather than errors in installed-package runs.
evidence: tests/unit/test_packaging_dependencies.py:22-25 `if not _PYPROJECT.is_file(): pytest.skip("pyproject.toml not present (installed-package test run)")`

The module docstring and fixture explicitly anticipate installed-package runs where pyproject.toml is absent; this test does not take the `pyproject` fixture and will error rather than skip in that environment.
advisory.finding: The new test reads `_PYPROJECT.read_text()` directly (line 123) instead of using the module `pyproject` fixture, so it bypasses the fixture's `pytest.skip("pyproject.toml not present (installed-package test run)")` guard and will raise `FileNotFoundError` in an installed-package test run, unlike every sibling test in this module.
scenarios: Running the test suite against an installed package where pyproject.toml is not present on disk.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add the `pyproject` fixture as a parameter and use it: `def test_the_research_corpus_is_excluded_from_both_distributions(pyproject) -> None:` then `build = pyproject["tool"]["hatch"]["build"]["targets"]`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen or clarify the wheel-side assertion so it actually demonstrates the wheel cannot ship evals (e.g. assert packages are all under src/rebar), or scope the test name/docstring to the sdist.
evidence: The wheel exclude list (pyproject.toml:378-388) excludes infra but not evals; the wheel never shipped evals because it is outside the package root, so asserting the literal string 'evals' is absent from a single-element ["src/rebar"] list proves nothing about evals exclusion.
advisory.finding: The wheel assertion `"evals" not in build["wheel"]["packages"]` is a near-tautology: `packages = ["src/rebar"]`, so the check can never meaningfully fail and does not actually verify the wheel excludes the evals corpus (the wheel omits evals because it is outside src/rebar, not via any exclude entry), weakening the test's stated 'both distributions' guarantee.
scenarios: A future change that adds an evals package root or wheel include would not be caught by this assertion in its current form.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Build the sdist (and wheel) and assert no evals/ path (e.g. evals/README.md) is present in the archive, rather than grepping the exclude-pattern strings out of pyproject.
evidence: tests/unit/test_packaging_dependencies.py:128-133: `sdist_exclude = build["sdist"]["exclude"]` / `for pattern in ("/evals", "evals", "evals/**"): assert pattern in sdist_exclude`

Commit message: 'Building the sdist at the pre-move commit shows it already shipped docs/experiments/README.md and its siblings' — the defect is an observable build-contents fact, but the test never builds an sdist and so cannot observe it.

Refactoring-violation: a behavior-preserving config change (e.g. a single consolidated `evals/**` glob, or a different hatchling exclusion mechanism) that still excludes the corpus would break this test despite identical distribution contents.

Regression-blindness: the motivating bug is that the config READS like it excludes evals/ while the build still ships it; asserting the config strings are present cannot distinguish a working exclusion from a hatchling glob-semantics change that reships the corpus.
advisory.finding: The new test asserts the literal presence of exclude-pattern strings in parsed pyproject TOML rather than the observable outcome (that a built sdist omits the evals/ corpus). It is a change-detector and is blind to the exact regression the diff fixes: the include allowlist's depth-agnostic README.md glob silently shipping research READMEs into the actual sdist.
scenarios: A future hatchling release changes exclude/include glob precedence so evals/ ships again despite the pattern strings still being present — test stays green.
Someone reorganizes the exclude list into an equivalent form — test breaks though no observable behavior changed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Drive the real build target (e.g. invoke `hatch build`/`python -m build --sdist` into a temp dir, or hatchling's sdist builder API) and assert that no member path under `evals/` appears in the produced sdist archive — and that at least one expected member (e.g. `src/rebar/...`) IS present, to anchor producer liveness.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the built wheel contains no evals/ member (inspect the produced wheel archive) instead of checking the literal `packages` config list.
evidence: Commit message: 'The corpus-move change asserted that neither distribution carries an evals/ entry. The wheel did not.' — the wheel path was never the defect.
tests/unit/test_packaging_dependencies.py:127: `assert "evals" not in build["wheel"]["packages"]` asserts a literal-string absence from a two-element config list rather than any built-wheel content.
advisory.finding: The `"evals" not in build["wheel"]["packages"]` assertion targets static config where `packages = ["src/rebar"]` and the commit states the wheel never carried evals; it verifies a condition that was never at risk and does not exercise wheel build output.
scenarios: Wheel accidentally includes evals/ via an `artifacts`/force-include glob — this assertion on `packages` would not catch it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Build the wheel into a temp dir and assert no `evals/` path is among its members, mirroring the sdist check, so both distributions are verified by observable contents.
